title: HTTP/2 client context stitching and resilience layer for dropped streams
creator: Priya Shah
description: Implement a thin resilience layer in the SDK and client middleware to stitch tracing/context across HTTP/2 multiplexed streams and recover gracefully from truncated/merged header frames or dropped streams. Goal: preserve span ancestry and sampling decisions across stream resets, server-push responses, and gRPC-over-HTTP2 fanout patterns without significantly increasing latency or header size for typical requests. This ticket covers design, SDK changes (Node/Go/Rust), and test harness + e2e dashboarding for rollout.
acceptance_criteria: SDK middleware detects and re-associates orphaned child stream contexts to parent request when stream reset occurs (RST_STREAM) in >=95% of fuzzed scenarios
Sampling decision header persisted and honored across stream multiplexing and server-push responses
No more than 1ms median extra latency on typical 50ms requests in the Node SDK integration test suite
Automated e2e tests that simulate stream resets, header truncation, and server-push included in CI
Documentation updated with migration notes and header compatibility tables
technical_approach: Introduce a compact context token (base64, <=48 bytes) that encodes span-id, trace-id, sampling-bit, and short provenance tag
Middleware will attach an idempotent Reconstruction header (X-RW-CTX) on outbound requests; receivers attempt best-effort stitch when canonical trace header missing
Client-side backoff: when header size would exceed 512 bytes for a request, fall back to single-stream token and emit a diagnostic metric
Cross-language SDK adapters (Node/Go/Rust): shared serialization spec and test vectors in /docs/obs/http2-context-stitch-spec.md
Resilience module will keep a small LRU cache of recent parent tokens and replay them when child streams are observed without parent metadata
risks_and_tradeoffs: Extra header increases wire size and could impact MTU-sensitive paths — mitigated by compact token and header-size-based fallback
Best-effort stitching may introduce incorrect parent attribution in rare race conditions — mitigated by conservative expiry (200ms) and sampling revalidation
Cache introduces memory overhead in hot clients — bounded by LRU size (configurable, default 256 entries)
Requires security review due to new forwarded metadata header (no secrets, only IDs and sampling bit)
testing_plan: Unit tests for serializer/deserializer with canonical vectors (Node/Go/Rust)
Integration tests using our HTTP/2 fuzz harness (simulate RST_STREAM, HEADERS lost, server-push)
Load test scenario comparing latency distribution with and without resilience layer (k6 + internal perf cluster)
End-to-end QA on Dedicated staging region with canary traffic for two days before broader rollout
rollout_plan: Canary rollout: 2% of requests on staging -> monitor tracing fidelity dashboard
If stable, increase to 20% then 100% over 72 hours; rollback condition: >2x increase in 95th latency or >1% wrong-parent attribution rate
Post-rollout: add opt-out instruction and migration guide in Console docs
observability_and_alerting: New Grafana dashboard: 'HTTP2 Context Stitching' (panels: stitch_success_rate, orphan_span_rate, header_size_distribution, latency_delta)
Create alerts: stitch_success_rate < 98% for 5m, orphan_span_rate > 0.5% for 10m, header_size_p90 > 400 bytes
Synthetic checks: nightly fuzz-run results pushed to perf-cq dashboard for trend analysis
